atoms.text: Clothing was an important part of Maya society because it was a way to show off power and wealth.
Rich people wore colourful, cotton clothing and expensive jewellery made out of jade or gold. They were also the only ones who could wear feathers and jaguar skins.
The poor Maya would wear more simple clothing and jewellery made out of bone and wood.

atoms.a: Select the two characteristics of clothing worn by the rich Maya.
Which two materials were the jewellery of the poor Maya made from?

atoms.b: To make ((++clothes cakes)), farmers would plant cotton. Once it had grown, it was ((++harvested thrown_away)) and washed to prepare it for weaving.
Women were the ((++weavers farmers)) in Maya society, and still are today!
The women would dye the ((++cotton plastic)) lots of different ((++colours shapes)) and weave it together using a loom.

finish.text: Maya women would traditionally wear a garment called a huipil. It is a loose-fitting tunic with holes for the head and arms.
finish.sound: ssml: Maya women would traditionally wear a garment called a weepeal. It is a loose-fitting tunic with holes for the head and arms.

atoms.b: Maya women would also wear the traje, which consisted of the huipil and a ((++skirt hat)) with a belt. Both the huipil and traje ((++are_still_worn are_not_worn)) today.
atoms.sound: Maya women would also were the traahey, which consisted of the weepeal and a skirt with a belt. Both the weepeal and traahey are still worn today.
